[p-164] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat ar-Rum (The Romans)

God Most High says: ﴿God's promise. God does not fail His promise, but most people do not know﴾ ﴿They know an outward aspect of the worldly life, while they are heedless of the Hereafter﴾.

God Most High says: ﴿God's promise﴾. It is an absolute object (maṣdar mu'akkid li-nafsih), meaning it emphasizes itself, because His saying before it, ﴿They will be overcome, after their overcoming, they will overcome﴾, up to His saying, ﴿On that day the believers will rejoice in God's victory﴾ [ar-Rum: 3-5], is itself the promise, as is well known. That is, God has promised that promise as a promise.

In this noble verse, God Most High mentions four matters. The first: that He does not fail His promise.

The second: that most people, who are the disbelievers, do not know.

The third: that they know an outward aspect of the worldly life.

The fourth: that they are heedless of the Hereafter. These four matters have come explained in other places.

As for the first of them, namely that He does not fail His promise, it has come in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed God does not fail the appointment﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 31]. God has also made clear that His threat against the disbelievers is not failed either, in verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿He said, "Do not dispute before Me, for I had already sent forward to you the warning. The word is not changed before Me"﴾ [Qaf: 28-29].

The verification is that the word that is not changed before Him in this noble verse is His threat against the disbelievers.

And like His saying: ﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My threat was justly due﴾ [Qaf: 14], and His saying: ﴿Each one denied the messengers, so My punishment was justly due﴾ [Sad: 14]. His saying "haqqa" (was justly due) in these two verses means "was required and established," so its failure is impossible in any way.

[p-165] As for the second of them, namely that most people, who are the disbelievers, do not know, it has come explained in many verses. God has made clear in verses that most people are disbelievers, such as:

- His saying: ﴿But most people do not believe﴾ [Hud: 17],
- His saying: ﴿And most of the earlier people had gone astray before them﴾ [as-Saffat: 71],
- His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them are not believers﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 8],
- His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray﴾ [al-An'am: 116],
- His saying: ﴿And most people, even if you should strive, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103],

and other verses besides these.

God Most High has also made clear in verses of His Book that the disbelievers do not know, such as:

- His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers did not reason at all, nor were they guided?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 170],
- His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers did not reason at all, nor were they guided?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 104],
- His saying: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve is like one who calls out to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry: deaf, dumb, blind, so they do not reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171],
- His saying: ﴿Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are only like livestock; rather, they are further astray in way﴾ [al-Furqan: 44],
- His saying: ﴿And We had certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray. Those are the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf: 179],
- His saying: ﴿And they will say, "Had we been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10],

and other verses besides these.

As for the third of them, namely that they know an outward aspect of the worldly life, it has also come in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them and averted them from the way, though they were discerning﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 38], meaning in the world, and His saying: ﴿So turn away from him who turns away from Our remembrance and desires only the worldly life. That is the extent of their knowledge﴾ [an-Najm: 29-30], up to the end of the verse.

As for the fourth of them, namely that they are heedless of the Hereafter, it has come in many verses, such as His saying about them: ﴿Far, far is what you are promised﴾ ﴿There is only our life of this world﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 36-37], up to the end of the verse.

And His saying about them: ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 35], ﴿And we will not be raised up﴾ [al-An'am: 29], ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]. The verses on this are many and well known.

* *

[Note] [p-166] Note.

Know that it is obligatory upon every Muslim in this age to reflect deeply upon this verse of ar-Rum, and to explain what it indicates to everyone among the people whom he is able to explain it to.

The clarification of that is that among the greatest trials of the last age, with which God has tested the weak-minded among the Muslims, is the great mastery of the Europeans (al-Ifranj) in the affairs of the worldly life, and their skill in them despite their multiplicity and the variety of their kinds, together with the Muslims' inability in that. So they thought that whoever is capable of those affairs is upon the truth, and that whoever is incapable of them is backward and not upon the truth. This is gross ignorance and a grave error. In this noble verse there is a clarification of this trial and a lessening of its importance, which God revealed in His Book many ages before it occurred. Glory be to the All-Wise, the All-Aware: how knowing He is, how great He is, and how excellent His teaching is!

God Most High has made clear in this noble verse that ﴿most people do not know﴾, and those who possess these worldly sciences enter into this at the first level. God Most High has denied them the name of "knowledge" in its true and complete meaning, because they know nothing about the One who created them, brought them from non-existence into existence, and provided for them, and who will cause them to die, then give them life, then recompense them for their deeds. They have not known anything about their final destiny, in which they will remain eternally in a terrible, perpetual punishment. Whoever is heedless of all this is not counted among those who know, as the Qur'anic verses mentioned indicate. Then, having denied them the name of "knowledge" in its true and complete meaning, God Most High affirmed for them a kind of knowledge that is extremely meager in comparison with other knowledge.

He faulted that mentioned kind of knowledge for two great defects. The first: its scantiness and the narrowness of its scope, because it does not go beyond ﴿an outward aspect of the worldly life﴾. Knowledge confined to an outward aspect of the worldly life is extremely meager and narrow in scope in comparison with knowledge of the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Glory be to Him, knowledge of His commands and prohibitions, of what brings His servant near to Him, what distances him from Him, and the deeds of good and evil that lead to eternal bliss or eternal punishment.

The second of the two: the baseness of the aim of that knowledge and the lack of nobility of its goal, because it does not go beyond the worldly life, which is swift to end and pass away. It suffices to show the contemptibility of this worldly knowledge that the best of the possible grammatical analyses (i'rab, grammatical parsing) of His saying ﴿they know an outward aspect﴾ is that it is a substitute (badal, apposition) for the preceding phrase "they do not know," so this knowledge is as good as no knowledge, because of its meanness.

[p-167] Az-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: "His saying 'ya'lamun' (they know) is a substitute (badal) for His saying 'la ya'lamun' (they do not know). In this substitution there is a subtle point: He substituted it for it and placed it in a position where it takes its place and fills its role, to teach you that there is no difference between the absence of knowledge, which is ignorance, and the presence of a knowledge that does not go beyond this world."

His saying ﴿an outward aspect of the worldly life﴾ indicates that the world has an outward aspect and an inward aspect. Its outward aspect is what the ignorant know of enjoying its adornments and indulging in its pleasures. Its inward aspect and its truth is that it is a passage to the Hereafter, from which one provisions oneself toward it through obedience and righteous deeds. The indefiniteness of "outward aspect" indicates that they know only one outward aspect of its outward aspects. As for "hum" (they) in the second position, it may be a subject (mubtada', grammatical subject) with "ghafiluna" (heedless) as its predicate (khabar), and the sentence is the predicate of the first "hum." It may also be a repetition of the first, with "ghafiluna" as the predicate of the first. Whichever it is, mentioning it indicates that they are the source of heedlessness of the Hereafter, its seat and its locus, and that it springs from them and returns to them. The words of the author of al-Kashshaf end here.

Others said: "The indefiniteness in His saying 'zahiran' (an outward aspect) reduces what they know, and this reduction brings it close to negation, so that it matches the substituted term." The meaning of this is clear.

Know that Muslims are obliged to learn these worldly sciences, as we have clarified in the fullest clarification in Surat Maryam, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Has he known the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Gracious?﴾ [Maryam: 78]. When Muslims learn these worldly sciences, whose meanness we have shown in comparison with what their disbelieving practitioners are heedless of, and when each of their teaching and use conforms to what God commanded through the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ), they become among the noblest and most beneficial sciences, because they are used to exalt the word of God and to seek His pleasure, Glory be to Him, and to reform this world and the Hereafter. There is then no fault in them, as God said: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾ [al-Anfal: 60]. Thus the work of preparing what one can of power, in obedience to God's command and in striving for His pleasure and the exaltation of His word, is not of the same kind as the knowledge of the disbelievers who are heedless of the Hereafter, as you see. The verses on the like of this are many. And knowledge is with God Most High.

(p-168) When the Exalted (jalla wa 'ala) explained that most people, namely the disbelievers, do not know, and then mentioned that they know an outward aspect of the worldly life while they are heedless, He denounced their heedlessness of the Hereafter, despite the great clarity of its proofs, by saying: ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term. Indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.﴾ The tafakkur (reflection) is contemplation and rational consideration. Its origin is the employment of thought (fikr). Later scholars say that fikr, in technical usage (istilah), is the movement of the soul over intelligibles (ma'qulat). Its movement over sensible things is, in technical usage, takhyil (imagination).

Al-Zamakhshari said in *al-Kashshaf*: ﴿within themselves﴾ may be a adverbial complement (zarf), as if it had been said: "Have they not produced reflection within themselves," that is, in their hearts, which are empty of thought. Thought exists only in the hearts, but this is an added depiction of the state of those who reflect, as in your saying: "He believed it in his heart, and concealed it in his self." It may also be a complement (silah) of tafakkur, as in your saying: "He reflected upon the matter," meaning he turned his thought over it. The phrase ﴿what God created﴾ is connected to a deleted verb of saying, meaning: "Have they not reflected, so that they would say this statement?" It was also said that its meaning is: "so that they would know," because the sentence contains an indication of it. ﴿except with truth and for a specified term﴾ means: He did not create them in vain or futility, without a correct purpose and a profound wisdom, nor to remain eternal. Rather, He created them accompanied by truth, joined with wisdom, and with a specified term appointed for them, to which they must inevitably come to an end, namely the establishment of the Hour and the time of reckoning, reward, and punishment.

Do you not see His saying: ﴿Did you suppose that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], how He called their leaving without returning to Him "vain." The ba' in His saying ﴿with truth﴾ is like it in your saying: "I entered upon him in traveling clothes," and "He bought the horse with its saddle and bridle," meaning: he bought it while it was accompanied by the saddle and bridle, not separated from them. Likewise the meaning is: He did not create them except that they are accompanied by truth and joined to it.

If you say: When ﴿in themselves﴾ is made a complement of tafakkur, what is its meaning? I say: its meaning is: "Have they not reflected within themselves, which are closer to them than other created things, and they are more knowing and more informed of their conditions than of the conditions of anything else? So let them contemplate what God has deposited in them, outwardly and inwardly, of the wondrous wisdoms indicating providential design and not neglect, and that they must come to an end at a time when the Judge who arranged their affair will recompense them: good for good, and the like for evil, so that at that time they will know that the rest of creation likewise has its affair proceeding according to wisdom and providence, and that it must come to an end at that time." The meaning of "meeting with their Lord" is the specified term. This ends the words of the author of *al-Kashshaf* regarding the interpretation of this verse.

What this noble verse indicates, that His creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them cannot be vain or futile, but rather He created them only with truth, is because if He had created them in vain, that vanity would be falsehood and play. Exalted is He above that, a great exaltation. Rather, He created them, and created everything in them and between them, only with truth. That is because He creates within them creatures, obligates them, commands them, forbids them, promises them and threatens them. Then, when the specified term for that comes to an end, He resurrects the creatures and recompenses them. Thus, in the believers, the attributes of His mercy, kindness, generosity, bounty, the vastness of His mercy and forgiveness become manifest, and in the disbelievers the attributes of His majesty, the severity of His seizing, the greatness of His punishment, and the intensity of His justice and equity appear. Many verses of the Book of God indicate this, such as His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ ﴿We did not create them except with truth, but most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all.﴾ [al-Dukhan: 38–40]. His saying ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment﴾ and the rest of the verse, after His saying ﴿We did not create them except with truth,﴾ clarifies what we have mentioned. And His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth, and indeed the Hour is coming.﴾

His saying ﴿And indeed the Hour is coming﴾ after His saying ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ clarifies that, and He has made it clear in His saying: ﴿And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best.﴾ [al-Najm: 31].

The Exalted has explained that those who think that He created them in vain, without wisdom, are the disbelievers, and He threatened them for that false assumption with woe from the Fire. That is in His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieved, so woe to those who disbelieved from the Fire.﴾ [Sad: 27]. The Exalted has also explained that if He did not resurrect the creatures and recompense them, then His creation of them in the first place would be in vain, and He declared Himself free of that vanity, Exalted is He above everything unfitting to His perfection and majesty, a great exaltation. That is in His saying: ﴿Did you suppose that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us?﴾ ﴿So exalted is God, the King, the Truth. There is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115–116].

These Qur'anic verses indicate that He, Exalted, did not create the creation except with truth, and that He will surely resurrect them and recompense them for their deeds, even though most of the people do not know this, so they were heedless of the Hereafter and disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord.

His saying, Exalted, in the mentioned verses: ﴿and what is between them﴾ means what is between the heavens and the earth. It includes the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth, the birds ﴿spreading their wings and folding them﴾ between the sky and the earth, and the air, without which living beings cannot do without breathing.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿they used to wrong themselves﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed it is on an established road﴾ [al-Hijr: 76]. And in al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Because of that, We decreed for the Children of Israel...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 32], the verse. And in Hud, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 83]. And in al-Isra', in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah﴾ [al-Isra': 17], the verse, and elsewhere.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this verse of al-Rum: ﴿They were greater than them in strength, and they stirred up the earth and cultivated it more than these have cultivated it﴾ [al-Rum: 9], it has come clarified in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in number and stronger in power and in traces left upon the earth, yet what they used to earn did not avail them﴾ [Ghafir: 82], and the like of that among the verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil was the worst (sū'ā), that they denied the signs of Allah and used to mock them.﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited this letter as ﴿kāna 'āqibatu﴾, with a damma on the tā' (the tā' of 'āqibah), so that 'āqibatu is the subject of kāna and its predicate is al-sū'ā. Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it as ﴿thumma kāna 'āqibata alladhīna﴾, with a fatha on the tā', so that 'āqibata is the predicate of kāna, placed before its subject, in accordance with the rule stated by Ibn Malik in the "Khulasah" (al-Khulasah, the versified grammar): "And in all of them the predicate may be moved to the middle; permit it..." (the verse is left incomplete in the text).

On this reading, al-sū'ā is the subject (ism) of kāna. The verb is stripped of the feminine marker (tā') even though al-sū'ā is feminine, for two reasons:

(p-171) The first: its feminine gender is not real (ḥaqīqī).

The second: the separation between it and the verb, as is well known.

As for the reading with a damma on the tā', the reason for omitting the feminine marker from the verb is only that the feminine gender of 'āqibah is not real.

The view I find most apparent regarding the meaning of the verse is that, on the reading with a damma on the tā', the meaning is: the end of the evildoers was the worst (al-sū'ā), which is the feminine form of al-asw'a (the superlative of evil), meaning: the one that is most evil. That is, their end was the punishment that is the worst of punishments, i.e., the most evil of them, and it is the Fire, from which Allah protect us and our Muslim brothers.

As for the reading with a fatha on the tā', the meaning is: al-sū'ā was the end of those who did evil. Its meaning is clear from what has preceded. The meaning of His saying "that they denied" is: their end was the worst of punishments because they denied.

This meaning is indicated by many verses which make clear that disbelief and denial may lead their evil consequence to the misery of the one who holds them and the evil of his end, we seek refuge in Allah:

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5],

• and His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10],

• and His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah sealed their hearts because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa': 155].

We have explained the verses indicating this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Isra': 46], and in "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾ [al-A'raf: 101], and elsewhere.

From what we have mentioned you will know that the view of one who said that ﴿so they were not to believe in what they had denied before﴾ is governed by asa'u (they did evil), meaning: they committed the evil crime, contrary to what is correct, and likewise the view of one who said that the "an" in His saying "an kadhdhabu" is interpretive (tafsiriyyah), is also contrary to what is correct. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Allah originates creation, then repeats it﴾.

We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in "al-Baqarah," "an-Nahl," "al-Hajj," and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will not be for them, among their partners, any intercessors﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And no intercession will be accepted from it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48], and elsewhere.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will be deniers of their partners﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! They will deny their worship and will be opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 81–82], and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs all praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you reach midday﴾.

We have already presented, in surah "al-Nisa'" (the Women), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾, that His saying here: ﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening﴾ and the two verses are among the verses in which the times of the five prayers are alluded to. We clarified the reason for this, along with clarifying all the verses in which the times of the five prayers are alluded to.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He brings the earth to life after its death. And thus you will be brought forth.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in our discussion of the proofs of resurrection (al-ba'th) in Surat al-Baqarah, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And sent down from the sky water, and produced thereby fruits as provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22]. And in Surat al-Nahl, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, the olive and the date palm﴾ [al-Nahl: 11], and elsewhere.

Allah's statement: ﴿And among His signs is that He created you from dust﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Ta-Ha, in the discussion of His statement ﴿From it We created you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55], and elsewhere.

Allah says: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And Allah made for you mates from among yourselves﴾ [al-Nahl 16:72].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 22:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed, in that are signs for those of knowledge.﴾

(p-173) His saying: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾: We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. As for His saying: ﴿and the diversity of your languages and your colors﴾, Exalted is He has explained in another place that the diversity of human colors, and the diversity of the colors of mountains, fruits, beasts and livestock, are all among His signs that point to the perfection of His power and to His worthiness of being worshipped alone. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying colors, and [others] extremely black. And among people and creatures and livestock are those of varying colors likewise﴾ [Fatir: 27-28]. The diversity of the colors mentioned is among the wonders of His creation and His marvels, and among the decisive proofs that He is the One who effects (everything), exalted is He, and that attributing effect to nature is among the greatest disbelief and error.

Allah, Exalted is He, has also clarified the nullification of the effect of nature in the utmost clarity in Surat al-Ra'd: ﴿And on the earth are neighboring tracts...﴾, up to His saying: ﴿for a people who reason﴾ [al-Ra'd: 4]. This letter was read by Hafs alone from 'Asim: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for those of knowledge﴾ with a kasrah on the lam, as the plural of ʿālim (knower, the opposite of ignorant). The rest read it (lil-ʿālamīn) with a fatha on the lam, as in His saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Banu Isra'il" (Al-Isra'), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day illuminating, that you might seek bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Isra': 12], and in Surah "al-Furqan" (Al-Furqan), and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that He shows you the lightning, as a fear and as a hope﴾.

We have already presented what clarifies this from the verses, together with the explanation of His saying ﴿as a fear and as a hope﴾, in Surat "al-Ra'd" (Surat al-Ra'd, the Thunder), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who shows you the lightning, as a fear and as a hope﴾ [al-Ra'd: 12] and so on. Here we will omit some of the cross-references because there are so many of them.

(p-174) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has coined for you an example from yourselves: Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you?﴾ and so on.

We have already presented its clarification from the Qur'an in Surah "al-Nahl," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision﴾ and so on [al-Nahl: 71].

[p. 364]

In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat ar-Rum

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth﴾ [30:30], and the rest of the verse.

This is an address specifically to the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah, may He be exalted, then said: ﴿turning back to Him, and fear Him﴾ [30:31]. His saying ﴿turning back to Him﴾ is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, describing the state of the subject at the time of the action) of the concealed subject pronoun in His saying ﴿So direct your face﴾, which refers to the Prophet (ﷺ). The meaning is therefore: "So direct your face, O Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while you are ones ﴿turning back to Him﴾."

It is established among the scholars of Arabic grammar (ʿArabiyya) that if the ḥāl is not a sababiyya (a ḥāl expressing cause), it must agree with its ṣāḥib (the word it describes) in number (singular, dual, plural) and in gender (masculine, feminine). So what is the explanation for the combination of this ḥāl, which is plural, with its ṣāḥib, which is singular? The answer is that the address specific to the Prophet (ﷺ) has a ruling that applies to the entire ummah, so the ummah enters under his address (ﷺ), and the ḥāl is therefore a state of all those who fall under his address (ﷺ).

A parallel to this verse, in which the ummah enters under an address specific to him (ﷺ), is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [65]. His saying ﴿when you (plural) divorce women﴾ after ﴿O Prophet﴾ is evidence that the ummah enters under the word "Prophet." Also His saying ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit﴾ [66], then He said: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ [66:2]. And His saying ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾ [33:1], then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ [33:2].

And His saying: ﴿So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you﴾ [33:37], then He said: ﴿so that there will be no discomfort for the believers﴾ [33:37], and the rest of the verse.

And His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter﴾ [10:61], then He said: ﴿nor do you do any deed﴾ [10:61].

The entry of the ummah into the address specific to the Prophet (ﷺ) is the position of the majority (al-Jumhur), and it is the view of Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa and Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on them, in contrast to al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him.

Allah's statement: ﴿And whatever you give in usury (riba) so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with Allah﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Baqarah," in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Allah destroys interest (yamhaqu Allahu al-riba)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 276] and what follows it.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿On that Day they will be divided﴾.

That is, they will separate into two groups: one in Paradise, and the other in the Fire.

Verses of the Book of Allah indicate this, such as His saying in this noble surah: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾. ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, made joyful﴾. ﴿But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought forth into punishment﴾ [al-Rum: 44-45]. And His saying: ﴿and to warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt: a group will be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shura: 7]. His saying after it supports this: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief; and whoever does righteousness, for themselves they prepare [a resting place]﴾ ﴿So that He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds from His bounty. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾ [al-Dukhan: - 45]. The Almighty has also alluded to the separation mentioned here in His saying: ﴿On that Day people will depart in scattered groups to be shown their deeds﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 52:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾, up to His saying: ﴿You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims [in submission]﴾.

We have already presented the clarifying verses in surah "An-Naml" (the Ant), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear﴾ [An-Naml: 80], the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾.

(p-175) Allah, may He be exalted, has explained the first weakness from which He created them in verses of His Book, and He explained the final weakness in other verses. In the first, He said: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20]. He said: ﴿He created man from a drop, and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4]. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop?﴾ up to the verse [Ya-Sin: 77]. He said: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid﴾ [al-Tariq: 5-6]. He said: ﴿No indeed; We have created them from that which they know﴾ [al-Rum: 39], and other verses besides these.

He said of the second weakness: ﴿And among you is one who is returned to the most abject age﴾ [al-Nahl: 70], and He said: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Will they not reason?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 68], and other verses besides these. He indicated the strength between the two weaknesses in verses of His Book, such as His saying: ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4]. His applying the same word "weakness" to that from which He created man has been clarified, its manner, in the commentary on Surah al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ up to the verse [al-Anbiya': 37].

ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read ﴿min ḍaʿf﴾ (with a fatḥah on the ḍād, "ḍaʿf") in the three places, in the genitive and accusative cases, in all of them, while the rest read it with a ḍammah (ḍuʿf).

Ḥafṣ chose the reading with a ḍammah, in agreement with the majority, on account of the hadith transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), through the route of ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfi, that he, meaning Ibn ʿUmar, recited to him (ﷺ): ﴿min ḍaʿf﴾ with a fatḥah on the ḍād, and he (ﷺ) corrected him and commanded him to recite it with a ḍammah on the ḍād. The hadith was related by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it ḥasan, and others related it besides them. And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear that they had not remained but an hour. Thus were they deluded.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this matter in Surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them, [it will be as if they had not remained but an hour of the day]﴾ [Yunus: 45], and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained, according to the decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection; and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware."﴾

In this noble verse, exalted is He mentions that when the disbelievers are resurrected on the Day of Resurrection and swear that they did not remain except for an hour, those who were given knowledge and faith will say to them, and the angels, the messengers, the prophets, and the righteous are included among them: "By Allah, you have indeed remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware."

This meaning which this noble verse indicates is clarified in Surah Ya-Sin according to the more correct of the two interpretations, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52].

The verification is that this is the statement of the disbelievers concerning the resurrection, and the verse clearly indicates that they sleep a sleep before the resurrection, as stated by more than one scholar, and upon their being raised alive from that sleep, which is the sleep of death, those who were given knowledge and faith will say to them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52], i.e., this is the resurrection after death which the Most Merciful promised you through the tongues of His messengers, and the messengers spoke truly in that, as you have witnessed it with your own eyes. So His saying in Ya-Sin, ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised﴾, is the saying of those who were given knowledge and faith, with certainty, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and it corresponds to the meaning of His saying: ﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You have indeed remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection"﴾, and so on.

The verification is that His saying here refers to what the Most Merciful promised, and that these words are from the speech of the believers, and it is not a reference to the resting place in the saying of the disbelievers: ﴿Who has raised us from this our sleeping place?﴾. And His saying: ﴿According to the decree of Allah﴾, i.e., in what He wrote, decreed and ordained. Some scholars said: His saying ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised﴾, and so on, is the statement of the disbelievers, and His saying in Surah As-Saffat supports it: ﴿And they will say, "Woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense. This is the Day of Judgment"﴾, and so on [As-Saffat: 20-21].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and they will not be allowed to make amends﴾.

We have already presented what it contains of linguistic variants and Arabic evidence (shawahid) in Surat al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then they will not be permitted [to offer excuses], nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [al-Nahl: 84].

The Qur'an, verse 58 of Surah 30: "And if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, 'You are nothing but falsifiers.'"

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-An'am" (The Cattle), in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scroll, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieve would have said, "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾ [al-An'am: 7]. And in Surah "Bani Isra'il" (The Children of Israel), in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth."﴾ [al-Isra': 90]. (p-177) And in Surah "Yunus" (Jonah), in the discussion of His saying, ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe﴾ [the verse], [al-Fatiha: 69], and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 30, verse 60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾. We have already mentioned in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit reproached and forsaken﴾ [al-Isra' 17:22], that Allah, exalted is He, has made clear in some Qur'anic verses that He addresses the Prophet ﷺ with an address that does not mean the person of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself, but rather intends legislation (tashri', the establishing of rulings for the community).

We also explained that among the most explicit verses in this regard is His saying, exalted is He, addressing him ﷺ: ﴿Should one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Isra' 17:23]. It is well known that his parents had died long before the revelation of: ﴿Should one or both of them reach old age with you﴾. There is therefore absolutely no basis for conditioning this on their reaching old age, or on one of them reaching old age in his presence. Rather, the intent is the legislation of kindness to parents for his community, through his address ﷺ.

Know that the view of one who says that the address in His saying: ﴿Should one or both of them reach old age with you﴾ is directed to whoever is fit to be addressed among the responsible persons, and that it is like the saying of Tarafa ibn al-'Abd:

"The days will reveal to you what you did not know"

...is contrary to what is correct.

The evidence for this is His saying, after mentioning the items joined to His saying: ﴿do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra' 17:23], ﴿That is part of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you﴾ and the rest of the verse [al-Isra' 17:39]. It is well known that His saying: ﴿That is part of what your Lord has revealed to you﴾ is an address to him ﷺ, as you see. We have also mentioned some Arabic examples of addressing a person while the real intended party of the address is someone else.

By this you know that verses such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾,

• and His saying: ﴿If you were to associate partners with Allah, your deeds would surely be lost﴾ [al-Zumar 39:65],

• and His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾ [al-Insan 76:24],

• and His saying: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god﴾ [al-Isra' 17:22],

are meant as legislation for his community, because he ﷺ is protected from that disbelief which he was forbidden from.

* *

A benefit.

It has been narrated through more than one chain that Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, was called out to by a man from the Kharijites during the dawn prayer, and he recited: ﴿And it has certainly been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost, and you will surely be among the losers﴾ [al-Zumar 39:65]. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, replied to him while he was in prayer: ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾.
